title: Product of Array Except Self
prompt:
Return an array `answer` where `answer[i]` is the product of every element of `nums` **except** `nums[i]`. Solve it in O(n) **without division**.

**Example**: `[1,2,3,4]` → `[24,12,8,6]`.

**Constraints**: `2 <= nums.length <= 10^5`, `-30 <= nums[i] <= 30`; all intermediate products fit in an `int`. Follow-up: O(1) extra space (the output array doesn't count).
hints: Picture index i splitting the array into two parts. How does `answer[i]` relate to those two parts?
answer[i] = (product of everything left of i) × (product of everything right of i). Compute all left products in one sweep and all right products in another.
Fill `res` with prefix products left→right, then sweep right→left with a single running variable: `res[i] *= right; right *= nums[i];`

solution.explanation: Insight: the product of everything except `nums[i]` is the prefix product before i times the suffix product after i. The first pass stores each prefix product in `res[i]`; the second pass multiplies in the suffix product accumulated in `right`, which at index i covers exactly `nums[i+1..n-1]`. No division means zeros need no special casing. O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
